tags.name: Yatouche
tags.qa_notes: UNRESOLVED (re-audited 2026-08-10, status unchanged): Coordinates fall near Israel-Jordan maritime boundary. All sources for Yatush wreck (Hebrew: יתוש) locate it at Eilat, Israel — ahla-dive.com specifies it is ~400m south of the Sufa wreck, in front of Aqua Sport Diving Center, Eilat. Not found in any Jordanian dive site listing. Possible OSM boundary error. Jurisdiction unconfirmed — do not present as a confirmed Jordanian dive site.

tags.name: Cedar Pride
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-10, all core facts reconfirmed, no corrections needed. Built 1964 Gijón Spain. Names: Mone Dos → Puerto De Pasajes → San Bruno → Cedar Pride. Length 74m (some sources say 'around 80m' for wreck extent). Tonnage conflict persists: 1,161 GRT per most specific sources (also seen as ~1,100 tons displacement in a fresh search) vs ~2,500t in one earlier-reviewed source — conflict noted, not resolved. Fire 2 Aug 1982, scuttled 16 Nov 1985 by Crown Prince Abdullah (later King Abdullah II). Lies on port side, 10m–27m. Marine life (site-specific): lionfish, giant frogfish, clownfish, snapper, fusiliers, angelfish, moray eels, hawksbill turtles.

tags.name: סופה
tags.qa_notes: UNRESOLVED (re-audited 2026-08-10, status unchanged): Sufa/Satil (INS Sufa, Sa'ar 3 class) is documented by all sources as located in Eilat, Israel — adrex.com specifies Coral Beach; other sources say Village Beach (both Eilat, Israel; Wikipedia confirms Sa'ar 3-class hull length as 45m, consistent with adrex.com's 46m figure). Sink year still conflicts between sources: adrex.com states 1994, others state 1993 — unresolved, both noted. Coordinates (29.545N, 34.954E) fall near Israel-Jordan maritime boundary. Hebrew name tag in OSM. Not found in any Jordanian dive operator listing. Very likely an Eilat, Israel dive site erroneously scraped into Jordan bounding box. Jurisdiction unconfirmed.

tags.name: Japanese Gardens Coral Reefs
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-10. Reef starts shallow (1-2m), slopes to Black Coral Valley at 26-30m. Large gorgonian fan at 23m, home to yellowmouth morays and large cornetfish (new site-specific detail from thenextcrossing.com). Coral relocation from Saudi border in 2013 confirmed. Marine life (site-specific): hawksbill turtles, sergeant majors, fusiliers, moray eels, lionfish, anthias, barracuda (added — confirmed by thenextcrossing.com), occasional white-tip reef sharks in deep blue.

tags.name: Gorgon 1
tags.qa_notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-10: Re-audit found the previous pass's 'two fans, not one' correction is itself contradicted by fresh sources. Sources now conflict on fan-coral count: arabdivers.jo verbatim says 'the single, massive gorgonian fan coral' and freedivingjordan.wordpress.com (independent diver blog, not a dive shop) says 'the huge Gorgonia fan coral at 16m' (singular); jordan-travel.com verbatim says 'Other two large Gorgonia corals are there, thus name Gorgone was given' (plural). Genuinely unresolved 1-vs-2 conflict — noting both rather than asserting either. ALSO CORRECTED: entry_type changed from 'boat' to 'both' — no fresh source describes boat-only access; jordan-travel.com explicitly lists 'Access: From shore/From boat' and gives a shore entry description (3m wide, 4m deep channel through fringing reef), and freedivingjordan.wordpress.com independently describes a 'zig zag entrance thru fringing reef'; arabdivers.jo lists 'Shore' as the access platform. No source found describing boat-only access, so the prior 'Primary boat access' note was unsupported. Three pinnacles rising to surface, 10-18m. Cabbage coral the size of a house at base of third pinnacle. Marine life (site-specific): hawksbill turtles, big-eye emperors, sergeant majors, fusiliers, glassfish, lionfish, stonefish, yellowmouth moray, grouper, cleaner shrimp (added — confirmed via arabdivers.jo).

tags.name: Tank
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-10, all facts reconfirmed. M42 Duster anti-aircraft vehicle, sunk 1 Sep 1999 by Jordanian Royal Ecological Diving Society. 6m depth, 20m from shore. Prior markdown claim of '1965 to 1998' Jordanian Army service REMOVED — no independent source confirms these specific dates. Marine life (site-specific): lionfish, angelfish, groupers, moray eels.

tags.name: Plane wreck
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-10. Lockheed C-130 Hercules, donated by Royal Jordanian Air Force, scuttled 16 Nov 2017. Length 30m, wingspan ~40m. Located ~300m from shore (reconfirmed directly on arabdivers.jo). Max depth 12-17m. Plastic skeleton in pilot seat confirmed. Storm damage confirmed and re-verified 2026-08-10 via deepbluedivecenter.com direct fetch: storm hit 17 March 2020, wings sank to bottom, fuselage torn in two, nose section detached to a separate location, tail remained intact. Note: one source (Dive Magazine article) initially listed 2021 but multiple sources confirm 2017.

tags.name: Rainbow reef
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-10. Arc-shaped reef, 6-18m. Four telecommunications cables laid 1996 (Jordan-Egypt) run beneath reef — northern and southern walls are steel-netted/shored artificial structure built to protect cables (reconfirmed). New detail confirmed by two independent sources (WebSearch summary + direct fetch of ermakvagus.com): night dives require 12 hours' advance notice and Jordanian Navy presence for safety, typically scheduled 6-9pm. Known as Aqaba's top night dive site. Marine life (site-specific): Spanish dancers, lobsters, feather stars, moray eels, lionfish, parrotfish, butterflyfish, wrasse, scorpionfish, eagle rays.

tags.name: אתר צלילה -סטי"ל (24 מטר)
tags.qa_notes: CRITICAL, re-audited 2026-08-10 (status unchanged): OSM coordinates (29.5145N, 34.9270E) are within ~30m of the Israeli Satil/Sufa wreck at Village Beach, Eilat. The OSM name tag in Hebrew reads 'Diving site - Satil (24m)'. This OSM entry almost certainly represents the Israeli Satil/Sufa wreck, NOT Jordan's Underwater Military Museum. The real Underwater Military Museum is off South Beach, Aqaba (SOUTH of city center, consistent with divernet.com's 2026-08-10 description). This entry's name has been set to 'Underwater Military Museum' in a previous community pass but the coordinates and Hebrew tag strongly indicate it is the Israeli Satil. Requires coordinate correction before this can be treated as a confirmed Jordanian UMM entry. The UMM itself is well documented: 19-21 vehicles (divernet.com's fresh summary lists 21, consistent with prior range), FV701 Ferrets, FV101 Scorpions, Chieftain/Khalid tanks, Chieftain ARV, FV103 Spartan, FV104 Samaritan ambulance, Ratel-20, M1 155mm guns, Willis jeeps, M42 Duster, 2x Bell AH-1F Cobra helicopters. Inaugurated 25 Jul 2019. Depths 5-28m. Marine life (site-specific): garden eels, moray eels, scorpionfish, bannerfish, reef fish, nudibranchs.

UPGRADED 2026-08-10: previous 'moderate confidence / no site-specific species list confirmed' hedge was overly cautious. Direct fetch of arabdivers.jo's own 'Coral Garden' dive-site page (the exact same source already listed in validation_source, but apparently not fully checked in the prior pass) confirms this site by name and lists site-specific marine life: moray eels, frogfish, crocodilefish, torpedo rays, barracuda, pufferfish, clownfish, and reef fish schools — closely matching the markdown's existing species list. Torpedo ray added as a newly confirmed species; all other listed species reconfirmed. Also newly confirmed: located in front of Aqaba's electricity/power plant on the southern coastline within the protected marine park; medium-strong currents; depth to 18m; access can be restricted by gated hotel-adjacent areas requiring local operator guidance (same pattern as Kiwi Reef).

Re-audited 2026-08-10, reconfirmed and strengthened. First Bay South at these coordinates. Descends to 30m recreational, with the technical 'Death Valley' section beyond 40m independently documented on its own dedicated page (diveaqaba.com/dive-site/death-valley) — strong downward currents pulling divers past 100m confirmed by a second source. Largest cabbage corals in the Middle East reported. Note: 'whale sharks' mentioned in one source for this site but not corroborated by other local operators — treat as occasional/unconfirmed.

UPGRADED 2026-08-10: previous thorny-seahorse hedge is resolved. muchbetteradventures.com and aqaba-diving.com independently confirm a seagrass bed at this site 'prowled by lionfish, scorpionfish, and several species of seahorse,' and a good spot to see 'seahorse and pipefish' — this now counts as site-specific confirmation of seahorses in the Blue Coral seagrass, not just a regional plausibility claim. Three finger reefs perpendicular to shore (depth range 10-25m per multiple sources; one source states up to 50m for the reef spurs — deeper figure not corroborated, flagged as a possible extent-vs-max-depth difference). Named for blue Acropora formations. Known nudibranch site. Marine life (site-specific confirmed): turtles, morays, rays, nudibranchs, shrimpfish, seahorses (including reports consistent with thorny seahorse habitat), pipefish, lionfish, scorpionfish.

Re-audited 2026-08-10, reconfirmed. Named for a New Zealand diver (Bevan Airey) who discovered it. Dozen+ coral pinnacles over seagrass, main cluster 10-20m (one source separately describes a deeper pinnacle cluster around 30m — noted as a possible different feature/technical extension, not corrected in the absence of a source reconciling the two). Marine life (site-specific, reconfirmed): morays (described as exceptionally abundant, nursery conditions for juvenile fish), lionfish, stingrays, emperors, thorny seahorses specifically confirmed in seagrass fronds, triggerfish, fusiliers, damselfish. Noted as exceptional night dive and photography site.

Re-audited 2026-08-10, reconfirmed. Well documented via Seastar Watersports house reef (site sits ~50m from the dive center, per tribloo.com). Wall starts at 6m, drops to 80m+ (depth range 6-80m independently reconfirmed). Shallow sandy training area. Black coral trees at depth, garden eels at 30m confirmed. Aqaba's most popular night dive. Marine life (site-specific): grey morays, fusiliers, groupers, flounders, garden eels, scorpionfish, lionfish, frogfish, giant clams, shrimps, hawksbill turtles near north buoy.

Re-audited 2026-08-10. Jordan's southernmost dive site, ~25 min drive from Aqaba town, 4km south of the Royal Diving Club. 850m wall extent reconfirmed. Wall crest/drop-off depth has a source conflict: earlier-reviewed sources describe a 12-15m plateau before the drop; scubatravel.co.uk (newly checked) describes the wall starting at 7-8m and running to 40-60m. Both figures noted rather than picking one — likely reflects different starting points along the 850m wall. Best area is shallow cabbage coral plateau before wall drop. Marine life (site-specific): humphead wrasse, turtles, hunting jacks, sharks and moray eels reported (sharks/morays reconfirmed independently by scubatravel.co.uk). Access to far southern section may require special arrangements.
